import re
s = open('"'"'losses.py'"'"').read()
start = s.index('"'"'def loss_fn_rl'"'"')
new = r'"'"''"'"''"'"'def loss_fn_rl(hidden, head, batch, correction=None, chunk=128):
    """Sampler-centered REINFORCE loss on sampled rollouts, with an optional
    ISCorrection. Returns (loss, metrics).

    Each token'"'"'s score w(y) * grad log p(y) is centered by its expectation
    under the sampler q at the same context,
        c_t = w(y_t) grad log p(y_t) - sum_v q(v) w(v) grad log p(v),
    so that E_{y_t ~ q}[c_t | context] = 0 for any q, as the plain score is
    on-policy (sum_v p(v) grad log p(v) = 0). Without this, any advantage
    offset that does not depend on the token (a group baseline, plus_minus
    rewards, the value of the context) multiplies E_q[grad log p] =
    -grad CE(q, p) != 0 and drags p along the mismatch direction q - p at
    every step, a drift that compounds as the sampler is refreshed from the
    trainer (REPORT.md). On-policy the centering term is exactly zero, so
    the loss reduces to REINFORCE.

    q is known on the sampler'"'"'s top-k tokens (sampler_topk_ids/logprobs); the
    remaining mass q_tail = 1 - sum_topk q is one "tail" outcome with trainer
    probability p_tail = 1 - sum_topk p, whose score is grad log p_tail.
    Without top-k logprobs the centering falls back to the sampled token only
    (plain REINFORCE).

    hidden [B, T, D] are pre-head activations and head maps them to logits.
    The head, log-softmax and all full-vocabulary float32 intermediates run in
    rematerialized chunks of `chunk` positions, so only [B, chunk, V] is live.

    batch: tokens, mask (completion tokens), advantages [B],
    sampling_token_logprobs [B, T], the sampler'"'"'s logprobs of the sampled
    tokens, and optionally sampler_topk_ids / sampler_topk_logprobs [B, T, K].
    """
    c = correction
    token_c = c if c and c.level == "token" else None
    seq_c = c if c and c.level != "token" else None
    targets = jnp.roll(batch["tokens"], -1, axis=1)
    mask = jnp.roll(batch["mask"], -1, axis=1).at[:, -1].set(False)
    positive = batch["advantages"][:, None] >= 0
    seq_len = targets.shape[1]
    chunk = next(n for n in range(min(chunk, seq_len), 0, -1) if seq_len % n == 0)
    centered = "sampler_topk_ids" in batch and "sampler_topk_logprobs" in batch
    sampler_keys = ("sampling_token_logprobs", "sampler_topk_ids", "sampler_topk_logprobs")
    per_token = {"hidden": hidden, "targets": targets, "mask": mask} | {k: batch[k] for k in sampler_keys if k in batch}

    def chunk_sums(start):
        b = {k: jax.lax.dynamic_slice_in_dim(v, start, chunk, axis=1) for k, v in per_token.items()}
        logp_vocab = jax.nn.log_softmax(head(b["hidden"]).astype(jnp.float32))
        logp = take_vocab(logp_vocab, b["targets"][..., None])[..., 0]
        logq = b["sampling_token_logprobs"].astype(jnp.float32)
        tv = sg(jnp.abs(jnp.exp(logq) - jnp.exp(logp)))
        w = is_weight(logp - logq, positive, token_c, tv)
        score = w * logp
        baseline = jnp.zeros_like(logp)
        tail_q = jnp.zeros_like(logp)
        if centered:
            # E_q[w grad log p] over the sampler'"'"'s top-k tokens plus one tail outcome
            ids = b["sampler_topk_ids"]
            logq_k = b["sampler_topk_logprobs"].astype(jnp.float32)
            logq_k = jnp.where(jnp.isfinite(logq_k), logq_k, -jnp.inf)
            logp_k = take_vocab(logp_vocab, ids)                       # [B, C, K]
            q_k = jnp.exp(logq_k)
            q_tail = jnp.clip(1.0 - q_k.sum(-1), 0.0, 1.0)
            p_tail = 1.0 - jnp.exp(logp_k).sum(-1)
            has_tail = p_tail > 1e-6
            logp_tail = jnp.log(jnp.where(has_tail, p_tail, 1.0))      # double-where: finite grads
            q_tail = jnp.where(has_tail, q_tail, 0.0)
            pk = positive[..., None]
            w_k = is_weight(sg(logp_k) - logq_k, pk, token_c, sg(jnp.abs(q_k - jnp.exp(logp_k))))
            w_k = jnp.where(q_k > 0, w_k, 0.0)
            log_q_tail = jnp.log(jnp.maximum(q_tail, 1e-30))
            w_tail = is_weight(sg(logp_tail) - log_q_tail, positive, token_c, sg(jnp.abs(q_tail - jnp.where(has_tail, p_tail, 0.0))))
            w_tail = jnp.where(q_tail > 0, w_tail, 0.0)
            baseline = sg(q_k * w_k) @ jnp.ones(()) if False else (sg(q_k * w_k) * logp_k).sum(-1) + sg(q_tail * w_tail) * logp_tail
            tail_q = sg(q_tail)
        plogp = sg((jnp.exp(logp_vocab) * logp_vocab).sum(-1))  # policy entropy metric
        terms = {"score": score - baseline, "entropy": -plogp, "kl_samp_train": sg(logq - logp),
                 "masked": w == 0, "tv": tv, "tail_q": tail_q}
        return {k: (v * b["mask"]).sum(-1) for k, v in terms.items()}

    chunks = jax.lax.map(jax.checkpoint(chunk_sums), jnp.arange(0, seq_len, chunk))
    sums = {k: v.sum(0) for k, v in chunks.items()}  # per-sequence sums [B]

    n_tokens = jnp.maximum(mask.sum(), 1)
    advantages = batch["advantages"]
    frac_masked = sums["masked"].sum() / n_tokens
    if seq_c:
        seq_tokens = jnp.maximum(mask.sum(1), 1)
        log_ratio = -sums["kl_samp_train"]
        if seq_c.level == "seq_mean":
            log_ratio = log_ratio / seq_tokens
        w = is_weight(log_ratio, advantages >= 0, seq_c, sums["tv"] / seq_tokens)
        advantages = advantages * w
        frac_masked = (w == 0).mean()  # fraction of sequences
    loss = -(advantages * sums["score"]).sum() / n_tokens
    metrics = {k: sums[k].sum() / n_tokens for k in ("entropy", "kl_samp_train", "tail_q") if k in sums}
    metrics["pol_entropy"] = metrics.pop("entropy")
    metrics["sampler_tail_mass"] = metrics.pop("tail_q")
    return loss, metrics | {"frac_masked": frac_masked}
'"'"''"'"''"'"'
s = s[:start] + new
s = s.replace("baseline = sg(q_k * w_k) @ jnp.ones(()) if False else (sg(q_k * w_k) * logp_k).sum(-1) + sg(q_tail * w_tail) * logp_tail",
              "baseline = (sg(q_k * w_k) * logp_k).sum(-1) + sg(q_tail * w_tail) * logp_tail")
open('"'"'losses.py'"'"','"'"'w'"'"').write(s)
EOF

import sys, importlib.util, jax, jax.numpy as jnp, numpy as np
def load(p):
    s=importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("m"+str(abs(hash(p))),p); m=importlib.util.module_from_spec(s); s.loader.exec_module(m); return m
new=load('"'"'/workspace/losses.py'"'"'); old=load('"'"'/tmp/losses_orig.py'"'"')
B,T,D,V=4,6,8,30
k=jax.random.key(0); ks=jax.random.split(k,5)
h=jax.random.normal(ks[0],(B,T,D)); W=jax.random.normal(ks[1],(D,V))
tok=jax.random.randint(ks[2],(B,T),0,V); mask=jnp.ones((B,T),bool).at[:,:2].set(False)
lp=jax.nn.log_softmax(h@W); tgt=jnp.roll(tok,-1,1)
tl=jnp.take_along_axis(lp,tgt[...,None],-1)[...,0]
for K in (V,10):
  tlp,tid=jax.lax.top_k(lp,K)
  batch=dict(tokens=tok,mask=mask,advantages=jnp.array([1.,-1.,.5,-.5]),sampling_token_logprobs=tl,sampler_topk_ids=tid,sampler_topk_logprobs=tlp)
  for c in (None, new.ISCorrection(high=2.0,outside="clamp")):
    g1=jax.grad(lambda W: new.loss_fn_rl(h,lambda x:x@W,batch,c)[0])(W)
    g0=jax.grad(lambda W: old.loss_fn_rl(h,lambda x:x@W,batch,c)[0])(W)
    print(K, c is not None, float(jnp.abs(g1-g0).max()), float(jnp.abs(g0).max()), new.loss_fn_rl(h,lambda x:x@W,batch,c)[1])
EOF

docker exec -w /workspace sc-run-20261120-124027-exp-L2a bash -lc 'cd /workspace && cat > REPORT.md <<'"'"'EOF'"'"'
# Sampler-centered REINFORCE

## 1. What is wrong with the current loss

For one completion y = (y_1..y_T) with advantage A, the loss gives the update
(per token, in the logits z_t of the trainer at context x_t = (prompt, y_<t))

    g = A * sum_t grad log p(y_t | x_t),      d log p(y|x)/dz = e_y - p     (1)

with tokens drawn from the **sampler** q, not from p.

**On-policy (q = p).** The score has zero mean at every context:

    E_{y~p}[grad log p(y|x)] = sum_v p(v) grad log p(v) = grad sum_v p(v) = 0.   (2)

So any part of the advantage that does not depend on the token y_t
(the group mean, the +-1 offset of `plus_minus`, the value V(x_t) of the
current context) contributes nothing in expectation: only the part of A that
is correlated with the choice of y_t moves the policy. Writing
Q(x,v) = E[A | x_t = x, y_t = v] and V(x) = sum_v q(v) Q(x,v),

    E_p[g] = sum_t E_x[ sum_v p(v) Q(x,v) (e_v - p) ] = sum_t E_x[ p ⊙ (Q - V) ]   (3)

i.e. the logit of v rises iff v is better than average. This is the policy
gradient.

**Mismatched (q != p).** (2) no longer holds:

    m(x) := E_{y~q}[grad log p(y|x)] = sum_v q(v) grad log p(v)
          = -grad_theta CE(q(.|x), p(.|x)),     in logits: m = q - p != 0.    (4)

Then

    E_q[g] = sum_t E_{x~q}[ sum_v q(v) (Q(x,v) - V(x)) grad log p(v) ]   (policy-improvement part)
           + sum_t E_{x~q}[ V(x) * m(x) ]                                 (bias)          (5)

The second term is a **reward-independent drift**: in logit space it is
V(x)(q - p). It does not care which token is better; it only depends on the
sign of the (offset) value of the context:

* V(x) > 0 (e.g. good contexts, or `plus_zero`): p is pulled towards q,
  i.e. SFT on the sampler'"'"'s mistakes (dp moves along the perturbation).
* V(x) < 0 (bad contexts, failed rollouts, `plus_minus` early in training,
  any context whose value is below the group mean): gradient **ascent on
  CE(q, p)**, which pushes p away from q. CE(q,p) is unbounded above: it is
  maximized by moving p'"'"'s mass off the tokens q likes onto tokens q
  dislikes, in particular onto the long tail of unlikely tokens (where noise
  makes q < p or q > p systematically).

Group-centering does not remove it. With A_i = r_i - mean_j r_j,
sum_i A_i S_i = sum_i r_i (S_i - S_bar) and

    E_q[sum_i A_i S_i] = (G-1) Cov_q(r, S) = (G-1) (E_q[r S] - E_q[r] E_q[S]),

and E_q[S] = sum_t E[m(x_t)] != 0; moreover the group mean is a baseline for
the prompt only, while V(x_t) - b varies along the sequence, so every
later position carries the drift V(x_t) - b times m(x_t).

**Why it compounds.** The mismatch is a fixed map θ -> q_θ (fixed weight
noise, quantization, a stale copy). The drift (5) has the same direction
(q_θ - p_θ, signed by V) at every step, and after the update the sampler is
rebuilt from the new trainer, so the mismatch -- and the drift -- are
regenerated rather than consumed. The bias is therefore integrated over
training (linear accumulation in θ), not averaged out like zero-mean noise.
Once p puts mass on tail tokens, q (a perturbation of p) samples them, those
rollouts fail (V < 0), and the drift away from q gets stronger: collapse.

**Why IS/clipping only slow it.** A token weight w(y) changes the drift to
E_q[w grad log p] = sum_v q(v) w(v) grad log p(v). This is zero only for the
exact ratio w = p/q (then it is sum_v grad p(v) = 0); this is the only
weight of the form f(y) that zeroes it for all directions, since the
condition is q(v) f(v) / p(v) = const. Any truncation, clamping or dropping
(TIS, MIS, PPO, DPPO ...) reintroduces a nonzero
sum_v q(v)(w(v) - p(v)/q(v)) grad log p(v), and stronger clipping means a
larger departure from p/q, hence a larger drift -- which is why it can be
worse. Exact IS removes it but at a variance cost, and sequence-level
weights don'"'"'t center the per-token score at all.

## 2. The modification: center each token'"'"'s score under the sampler

Replace the per-token score by its **q-centered** version

    c_t = w(y_t) grad log p(y_t|x_t) - sum_v q(v|x_t) w(v) grad log p(v|x_t)       (6)

(w = 1 without a correction; w = the token IS weight when a token-level
`ISCorrection` is given). The surrogate loss is

    L = - (1/N) sum_i A_i sum_t [ w(y_t) log p(y_t) - sum_v sg(q(v) w(v)) log p(v) ],

with q and w detached. Properties:

1. **Zero-mean under q for any q:** E_{y_t~q}[c_t | x_t] = 0 by construction.
   Hence every token-independent part of the advantage (group mean,
   reward offset, V(x_t)) has zero expected effect again, exactly as
   on-policy, and the bias term in (5) vanishes:

       E_q[A sum_t c_t] = sum_t E_{x~q}[ sum_v q(v) (Q(x,v) - V(x)) w(v) (grad log p(v) - m_w(x)) ].

   With w = 1 in logit space this is sum_t E_x[ q ⊙ (Q - V) ]: compare (3).
   The logit of a token goes up iff it is better than average (under the
   sampler'"'"'s own advantage). It is a policy-improvement direction with no
   component along q - p that does not depend on reward, so there is
   nothing systematic to accumulate. The remaining off-policy error
   (q instead of p in the weighting q ⊙ (Q-V), and states drawn from q) is
   second order: it rescales the improvement direction per token but never
   has a sign independent of the reward; the fixed point "all advantages
   zero" is still a fixed point.

2. **Exactly REINFORCE on-policy:** if q = p, sum_v p(v) grad log p(v) = 0,
   so the extra term has zero gradient (verified numerically: gradients are
   identical to the original loss to 3e-8 when q = p).

3. **Composes with IS:** with exact w = p/q the subtracted term is
   sum_v grad p(v) = 0 (nothing changes); with clipped/truncated weights it
   removes exactly the drift sum_v q(v)(w(v) - p/q) grad log p(v) that the
   clipping creates.

4. **Not a KL penalty.** It does not pull p to q (that would be the
   biased term itself with a fixed sign); its expected contribution is
   zero, it only removes the conditional mean of the score.

Interpretation: the centering is a per-context, per-token control variate,
equivalent to replacing the logit-gradient e_y - p of the sampled token by
e_y - q. Plain REINFORCE uses p as the "expected one-hot", which is right
only when the tokens come from p.

## 3. Computing E_q with what the sampler returns

The sampler returns q only on its top-k tokens (k = 20, `sampler_topk_ids`,
`sampler_topk_logprobs`, present in both `train_rl.py` and `dev/mini.py`).
Let K be that set, q_tail = 1 - sum_{v in K} q(v), p_tail = 1 - sum_{v in K} p(v).
The tail is treated as one outcome, approximating q on the tail by
q_tail p(v)/p_tail:

    sum_v q(v) w(v) grad log p(v)  ≈  sum_{v in K} q(v) w(v) grad log p(v) + q_tail w_tail grad log p_tail.

In logits this is e_y - q~ with q~ = q on K and q_tail * p/p_tail on the
tail, so E_q[e_y - q~] = q - q~ is non-zero only *inside* the tail and sums
to zero there: the residual drift cannot move mass between the top-k and the
tail, or change the tail'"'"'s total mass; it is bounded by the tail mass of q
(typically ~1e-2). When q = p it is exact. The top-k logprobs are gathered
from the trainer'"'"'s log-softmax with the same `take_vocab` helper (TP-safe),
everything in float32, inside the existing rematerialized chunks; the cost is
a [B, chunk, 20] gather. Numerics: log p_tail uses a double `where` so that
positions where the top-k covers the whole vocabulary give zero, finite
gradients; non-finite sampler logprobs are treated as q = 0. If the batch has
no top-k logprobs the loss falls back to plain REINFORCE.

The token weight for the top-k and tail outcomes is computed with the
existing `is_weight` (detached), so `rl.is.*` token-level corrections stay
valid; sequence-level corrections still multiply the advantage as before.
Metrics add `sampler_tail_mass` (mean q_tail).

## 4. Sanity checks (dev/mini.py, 600 steps; not needed for the argument)

Mean reward of the last 50 steps, original loss -> centered loss:

| setting | original | centered |
| --- | --- | --- |
| default (noise 0.3, plus_minus), seed 0 | 0.58 | 0.87 |
| default, seed 1 | 0.58 | 0.85 |
| 50 extra tail tokens, seeds 0/1 | 0.00 / 0.00 (collapse) | 0.78 / 0.86 |
| 200 extra tokens, seed 2 | 0.00 (collapse) | 0.73 |
| 50 extra, noise 0.5 | 0.00 (collapse) | 0.52 (rising) |
| 50 extra, group_centered | 0.71 | 0.72 |
| 200 extra, TIS (high=2, clamp) | 0.59 (eval dips to 0.20) | 0.62 (no dip) |

## Configuration

No configuration changes are needed: the centering is active with the
default `correction=None`.

I changed `/workspace/losses.py` so each token's score is centred under the sampler's distribution. On the CPU dev setup it no longer collapses, and `/workspace/REPORT.md` has the reasoning and the math.

**What was wrong.** When tokens come from the trainer itself, a token's gradient averages to zero, so any part of the advantage that doesn't depend on which token was picked has no effect. That part includes the group mean, the ±1 reward offset and the value of the current context. When tokens come from a different sampler, that average becomes q − p in logit space. The update then picks up a term of V(x)·(q − p) that ignores reward and has a fixed sign. Where V < 0, that term does gradient ascent on the cross-entropy between sampler and trainer, which has no upper bound. The sampler is rebuilt from the trainer every step, so the same push repeats every step and adds up over training.

Importance weights remove this term only when the weight is exactly p/q. Any clipping or dropping brings it back, so stronger clipping can make things worse.

**The fix.** Each token's score is replaced by w(y)·∇log p(y) − Σ_v q(v)·w(v)·∇log p(v), with q and w held constant (w = 1 by default).
- Under the sampler, this averages to zero for any q. The expected update in logit space becomes q ⊙ (Q − V): a token's logit rises only if that token beats the average.
- When q = p the extra term is exactly zero. Gradients matched the original loss to 3e-8 in my test.
- The sampler's distribution is taken from the top-20 log-probs that both `train_rl.py` and `dev/mini.py` already return. The rest of the vocabulary is treated as one bucket, and the error this leaves is bounded by how much probability the sampler puts outside its top-20.
- It is on with the default `correction=None` and needs no configuration. Token-level `rl.is.*` corrections still work: the term then subtracts exactly the drift that clipping creates.
- If a batch has no top-20 log-probs, the loss falls back to plain REINFORCE.

**Results.** These come from short runs of `dev/mini.py`, 600 steps each, mean reward over the last 50 steps. None of this was tested on the GPU Qwen3/Countdown setup.

| Setting | Original | Centred |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Default, seeds 0 and 1 | 0.58 | 0.85–0.87 |
| 50–200 extra unlikely tokens, 3 seeds | 0.00 (collapse) | 0.73–0.86 |
| Weight noise 0.5 | 0.00 | 0.52, still rising |
| With TIS (`high=2`, clamp) | 0.59 | 0.62 |
| Group-centred rewards | 0.71 | 0.72 |

So the change helps a lot when the original loss collapses and changes little where it doesn't.
